thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: GeoDNS probe cluster reporting elevated DNS error rate in eu-north-1 (SERVFAIL + FORMERR mix)
oncall-bot: scope=redwood-prod, symptom=europe resolver errors, rate=40% (5m), impact=EU traffic steering

alex.s: oncall — I see the paging graph. No infra deploys in the last 3h. Hold off on config changes until we pick mitigation; starting triage.

priya: digging into probe logs. We're seeing a mix of SERVFAIL and occasional FORMERR from Cloudflare-authoritative names for several apex and service subdomains. Route53 authoritative still answers fine. No obvious rate-limits.

netops: sample from probe pool:

```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 service.redwood-inference.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: FORMERR, id: 51234
```
\npriya: confirmed. Direct queries to Cloudflare authoritative IPs replicate FORMERRs intermittently, other resolvers (Route53) OK. Could be CF-side parser bug or a malformed EDNS option from some middlebox.

sophie: client-facing 5xx spike ~22% for EU sessions, mostly at edge TLS handshake step because traffic can't reach preferred edge due to DNS failures. CS queue lighting up.

alex.s: mitigation options: a) change GeoDNS policy to route EU traffic to Route53-backed pool (regional failover), b) lower TTL to 30s to speed revert, c) add temporary client-side retry guidance in status page. We should prefer non-disruptive weighted routing, not full global switchover.

priya: agree — do weighted 70/30 -> route53/cloudflare to reduce blast radius. I'll prep the API patch.

alex.s: executing safer route now. Patch below; will apply in canary then global.

```
# canary patch geo policy for eu-north-1
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/geodns/policy/eu-north-1/canary \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"weights":{"route53-pool":70,"cloudflare-pool":30},"ttl":30}'
```
\nnetops: canary applied. Validating from two EU probe nodes.

(oncall-bot): config-change audit: user=alex.s, action=POST, target=geodns/eu-north-1/canary

priya: probing after canary:

```
$ for i in 1 2 3; do dig +short @8.8.8.8 service.redwood-inference.com; sleep 1; done
93.184.216.34
93.184.216.34
93.184.216.34
```
\nnetops: canary looks good. No FORMERR in these dig tests; edge 5xx rate down to ~8%.

sophie: I'm taking handoff. I'll keep the canary for 10m and if stable, promote to full policy. I'll also open CF support ticket with traces.

support: posting customer status: "Investigating DNS resolution issues impacting EU routing. Mitigation underway; traffic is being shifted to alternate routing. Updates to follow."

cust-success-bot: Status posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-110

alex.s: enabling short alert suppression for duplicate DNS probe pages to avoid wake/loop. Window 45m.

priya: CF ticket created with samples and timestamps. Case ID: CF-91234. Attaching dig outputs and probe raw logs.

cloudflare-bot: Ticket CF-91234 acknowledged by Cloudflare triage. Assigned to network engineering. ETA 30m.

sophie: promoting canary -> full policy now. Using same API but without canary flag.

```
curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood/api/geodns/policy/eu-north-1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"weights":{"route53-pool":70,"cloudflare-pool":30},"ttl":30}'
```
\n(oncall-bot): config-change audit: user=sophie, action=PATCH, target=geodns/eu-north-1

support: EU client 5xx down to 3%. CS triage teams notified and given the status link.

sophie: Cloudflare engineering responding; they see a parser regression in a subset of authoritative nodes and are rolling a fix. We'll keep weighted routing until CF confirms full fix and two full propagation cycles.

priya: logging follow-ups: 1) expand probe diversity (more resolver vendors + fewer co-located probes), 2) add automated failover test that simulates FORMERR/SERVFAIL and validates GeoDNS policy triggers, 3) update runbook with CF escalation steps and contact path.

alex.s: thanks — handing off monitoring to netops and support for customer comms. I'm going offline for 20m. If errors spike, call the pager and @sophie.

netops: monitoring. Will collect pcap/dig samples if CF asks.

sophie: 40m post start: Cloudflare reports rolling fix completed in EU region authoritative nodes. We observed gradual reduction of FORMERR traces. Keeping weighted routing and TTL 30s for one more hour to verify.

cloudflare-bot: Cloudflare engineering: "A recent validator change caused malformed EDNS handling in a subset of authoritative clusters. Patch deployed and rolling; we see resolution rates returning to normal."

oncall-bot: Incident state -> mitigated; monitor window active until 3280008723

sophie: final handoff notes: 1) postmortem to cover cause, CF coordination timeline, why canary helped, probe coverage gaps; 2) runbook update for weighted failover; 3) add quarterly DR test for GeoDNS failover; 4) confirm CF contact info in vendor book. I'll own the postmortem doc.

alex.s: great work. Closing active pager. If anyone wants to add to the postmortem, comment here or ping @sophie.

support: closing CS incident tasks; will follow up with affected customers and include status link and ETA for permanent closure.

sophie: closing thread — will circulate postmortem draft within 48h. Good work team."
